title: Diagnosis Decision Tree Trainer
description: Three failures cause most "it doesn't work" reports on the kit: a silent microphone, distorted audio, and a blank display. The chapter writes each as a flat decision tree: ask the first row's question; yes ends at that row's likely cause, quick test and fix, and no moves to the next row, so the cheapest questions rule out whole branches first.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Study Buddy

learningObjectives: The learner will differentiate the likely cause of each of 6 reported kit failures from three other causes in the same decision tree, choosing the correct cause for at least 5 of 6 cases.
prerequisites: flat line, backlight, sample rate, frame overrun, wire swap (all defined in the sections of this chapter above this block and in Chapters 4 and 8); the three diagnosis tables in this chapter, whose rows are named M1 to M6, A1 to A7, and D1 to D8.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Does a silent microphone always mean a broken microphone?
Can a program that runs with no error still have a wiring fault?
Why does each tree ask "Is it completely dark?" before anything else?
commonMisconceptions: (1) Any failure of the microphone means the microphone is broken. (2) A program that runs without an error has no wiring fault. (3) A dark screen is always a software bug. (4) The answer to a distorted sound is always to lower the volume.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all six cases. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
